items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: So on November 21st of '47, I went into the 845 Club in the Bronx with a small combo lead by Billie Kyle. We were all ex-Sy Oliver members... Freddie William was on tenor, George Duvivier on bass and Wallace Bishop on drums.

ctx.x: It was a swinging band because Sy knew how to make a band do that and he knew how to arrange numbers in a swinging tempo. He also bought arrangements and George Duvivier was an arranger in the Sy Oliver medium. Very few big bands used guitars in the rhythm section anymore except for Count Besie. But Sy had one which was a big help to the section and kept it from being jumpy or instable otherwise.

The only musicians in the band other than Sy that I had known before were Dickie and Henry Wells, Eddie Barefield, Lamar Wright,Sr., George Dorsey, Billie Kyle and Wallace Bishop. I had seen Freddie Williams but did not know him very well. Aaron Smith and I became quite friendly, and we used to have a few drinks together in the Turf bar which was down stairs under the Zanzibar, when we had our intermission. Sometimes we went to Beafsteak Charlie's on 50th Street near Broadway, where many musicians hung out.

One night I told Smittie as most everyone called Aaron, that I had been in Europe during a certain time and had recorded with a guitarist named Django Reinhardt and I was surprised when he told me that he knew of Django and considered him the greatest improvising guitarist that ever lived.
